stories.headline: Rays take advantage of error-prone Yankees to win ALDS Game 2
stories.summary: The Rays took advantage of four errors by the Yankees to win Game 2 on Monday night and take a 2-0 lead in their ALDS.
stories.body:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- Richie Palacios hit a two-run single in a four-run fifth inning, and the Tampa Bay Rays took advantage of New York's sloppy defense, beating Cam Schlittler and the Yankees 5-2 on Monday night to take a 2-0 lead in their American League Division Series.

The Rays are one victory from reaching the American League Championship Series. Game 3 in the best-of-five playoff is Wednesday night at Yankee Stadium.

"That's a byproduct of having a really good clubhouse and a bunch of selfless teammates," Rays manager Kevin Cash said. "They don't care who gets it done. They just want to get it done. The biggest cheerleaders are coming from the guys within the dugout. Good teams do not rely on just one or two people. We rely on all nine in the lineup, the guys on the bench and certainly our entire pitching staff."

Ben Rice hit a pair of homers for the Yankees, who committed four errors and are now on the verge of elimination -- which would extend their World Series drought to 17 seasons. They were dominated by Drew Rasmussen in the series opener and have scored just two runs in two games with three-time AL MVP Aaron Judge out of the lineup because of a calf injury.

The small-ball Rays chased Schlittler, the likely AL Cy Young Award winner, in the fifth -- aided by New York's defensive miscues.

Jonathan Aranda lined a single to start the inning, and Junior Caminero ripped a double to right-center. With the infield drawn in except second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr., who was standing several feet farther back on the dirt, Liam Hicks hit a bouncer to second that scored Aranda for a 2-1 lead. Chisholm's only play was at first because he wasn't all the way in like the rest of the infielders.

Chandler Simpson then hit a grounder that shortstop George Lombard Jr. booted, scoring Caminero to make it 3-1. It was initially ruled a hit and then changed to an error and eventually a fielder's choice. Brent Headrick replaced Schlittler and struck out Victor Mesa Jr. After Simpson stole second, Jonny DeLuca reached on a grounder when Lombard's throw to first was wide for New York's fourth error.

Palacios followed with a hard single to center that increased Tampa Bay's lead to 5-1.

"It was just one of those game things kind of compiled and stacked up on top of each other," Lombard said. "It wasn't ideal. We put ourselves in a bad spot."

That was plenty of support for one of the best bullpens in the majors.

Freddy Peralta allowed one run and three hits in 4⅔ innings, Cam Booser pitched out of a bases-loaded jam in the fifth and Ian Seymour gave up one run on Rice's solo shot in three innings. Bryan Baker finished with a perfect ninth for his second save in two games.

Schlittler, who was 14-6 with a 1.95 ERA and dominated Boston in the opener of the wild-card round, lasted 4⅓ innings. He allowed four runs -- two earned -- and six hits. Schlittler fanned only two.

Rice sent a 2-2 changeup into the right-field seats to tie it at 1-1 in the fourth, ending New York's scoreless drought in the ALDS. Rice hit 41 homers in the regular season. His drive awakened Yankees fans, who were drowned out by Rays fans in the ballpark until that point.

But a sellout crowd of 40,226 was mostly full of cowbell-ringing Rays fans who reveled in New York's misery.

Peralta retired the first two batters in the fifth before Austin Wells ripped a double and Ryan McMahon walked. Booser replaced Peralta and walked Rice to load the bases, but the lefty escaped trouble when Cody Bellinger flied out to the warning track in center.

The Yankees made three errors in the first inning, but Schlittler limited the Rays to one run. New York became the fourth team to commit three errors in the first inning of a postseason game and the first since the Oakland Athletics in Game 1 of the 1975 AL Championship Series against Boston, according to ESPN Research.

The projected starters for Wednesday's elimination game are lefty Max Fried (5-5, 2.80 ERA) for the Yankees and right-hander Nick Martinez (15-6, 3.10) for the Rays.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

stories.headline: Linus Ullmark exits in 'precautionary' move against Bruins
stories.summary: Senators goaltender Linus Ullmark exited his team's game at the Bruins after tweaking something when he was crashed into during the second period.
stories.body:
BOSTON -- Ottawa Senators goaltender Linus Ullmark exited his team's game at the Boston Bruins on Monday night after tweaking something when he was crashed into during the second period, according to coach Travis Green.

Backup Samuel Ersson replaced Ullmark in net for the third period.

"Precautionary," Green said. "We just felt it was best that we bring him out."

Ullmark was slow to get up after Boston forward JJ Peterka collided with him after getting shoved by Ottawa's William Eklund with 4:24 left in the second. Green said that was the collision that caused Ullmark to feel something was off.

Ullmark stopped all 15 shots he faced, and Ottawa led 4-0 when he departed. The 33-year-old Swede was back on the bench early in the third period, Ersson allowed one goal and the Senators beat the Bruins 4-1 to improve to 2-0 this season.

stories.headline: 'Best person': North Melbourne name Jaymie Graham as senior coach
stories.body:
North Melbourne has named Jaymie Graham as its next head coach, tasking the Fremantle assistant with lifting the Kangaroos off the bottom of the AFL ladder.

The highly-rated Dockers assistant is understood to have addressed the Kangaroos board on Monday following an impressive presentation during the selection process.

"I'm delighted to announce that Jaymie Graham is the new senior coach of our AFL team," said club president Sonja Hood in a letter to members. "As a coach, Jaymie is a process-driven leader with a quiet, grounded presence, sharp attention to detail, and a clear football vision.

"Outside of his exceptional character, he joins us with a proven skill set. He played a key role in West Coast's 2018 premiership success, and more recently he was the line coach for one of the competition's best forward lines at Fremantle as part of a high-performing program."

More to follow...

stories.body:
Chelsea lead the race for AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott, while Bayern Munich are bracing for tough contract talks with star winger Michael Olise. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Trending rumors

- Chelsea are leading the race to sign AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott, who is also attracting strong interest from Liverpool and Arsenal, as reported by The Telegraph. Elsewhere, TEAMtalk have suggested that Real Madrid are considering becoming involved in the race for the 23-year-old after watching him closely in recent weeks. Los Blancos have watched Scott at least three times, including his first England start in the Three Lions' 7-0 victory over Croatia.

- Bayern Munich are concerned about talks to renew Michael Olise's contract, as the winger hasn't yet told them if he even wants to stay in Bavaria, as reported by Sport Bild. The Bundesliga club is preparing for a very difficult negotiation with the representatives of the 24-year-old. One of the sticking points is that the France international wants a release clause in his new contract, something both Harry Kane and Jamal Musiala have. Bayern are willing to offer a mega contract that will run until 2032 but want an answer by next summer.

- Italian outlet Corriere dello Sport has offered an insight into the names Roma are looking at as they aim to sign a winger. In the summer, they looked at Stuttgart's Jamie Leweling and Chelsea's Jamie Gittens, who have both had a lack of game time since the summer transfer window shut so could be available for less than was demanded before. They also want Real Madrid's Endrick, hoping for a Donyell Malen-style deal where they have a loan with the option to make it permanent, and they aren't alarmed by AC Milan's interest. Frosinone's Giorgi Kvernadze is another player of interest.

- Juventus see Marseille midfielder Pierre-Emile Højbjerg as the leader Luciano Spalletti needs, as reported by La Gazzetta dello Sport. They have previously looked at Leon Goretzka and Franck Kessié, who ended up at Aston Villa and Atalanta respectively, but remain keen on signing an older head for their midfield so are turning to the man who is captain for both Marseille and Denmark. There have already been exploratory contacts made about the 31-year-old, while Teun Koopmeiners is the main candidate to leave so he can come in.

- Juventus have recently made a move for Frosinone goalkeeper Lorenzo Palmisani and Inter Milan are monitoring him, as reported by La Gazzetta dello Sport. Inter chief executive Beppe Marotta has insisted on a mix of foreign and Italian players, emphasizing the importance of a strong Italy squad. I Nerazzurri could decide to loan out the 22-year-old if they sign him, and they are also looking at Alessandro Romano, who is on loan at Cagliari from Roma.

Other rumors
- Liverpool and Chelsea have joined the race to sign Nottingham Forest center back Murillo in 2027. (Football Insider)

- Leeds United are preparing to reject any potential approaches for Tarik Muharemovic with Barcelona and Inter Milan among the clubs tracking the center back. (Football Insider)

- Tottenham Hotspur could move for Kim Min-jae in the summer with Bayern Munich open to offers for the center back. (Football Insider)

- Premier League clubs have been monitoring Sevilla midfielder Lucien Agoume, who has a €40m release clause. (AS)

- Real Madrid have made significant progress in talks with Jude Bellingham over a new contract for the midfielder. (TEAMtalk)

stories.headline: State of each position in 2026: What are the biggest tactical trends?
stories.summary: Elite soccer has changed dramatically in recent years, and the most valued player skill sets have evolved as a result.
stories.body:
Elite European soccer in 2026 feels decidedly different from what we've become used to. Over the past couple of seasons, the Premier League has been increasingly characterized by direct attacking, set pieces and long throw-ins. Many encounters between big clubs across Europe have become frenetic, end-to-end affairs, such as the Bayern Munich-Paris Saint-Germain semifinals in last season's UEFA Champions League.

A lot of the changes seem related to how teams play without the ball. The soccer we became accustomed to throughout the 2010s involved top sides trying to push their opponents back while keeping the ball. Once the ball reached the attacking third, they tried to outnumber defenders in key spaces and make use of their attacking talent.

One way for defensive sides to counter this approach is to use zonal marking, which involves defending space rather than individual players. They would set up in compact blocks and deny space in critical areas, whether they defended deep like Max Allegri's Juventus in the 2010s or pressed high like teams coached by Ralf Rangnick's disciples. While this tactic helps protect the areas closer to goal and prevent mismatches, it sometimes plays into the hands of those high-possession sides.

As a result, player marking (or man-to-man marking), in which defenders are assigned to follow attackers around up and down the pitch, started to make a comeback at the turn of the 2020s. Teams like Mikel Arteta's Arsenal and Andoni Iraola's Bournemouth combined this concept with their zonal marking, switching out of a zonal structure in certain situations to swarm teams attempting to move the ball forward (hybrid pressing). This makes moving the ball slowly up the pitch harder, causing teams to embrace more direct approaches with the ball.

Meanwhile, the game appears to be becoming more physical and more intense. Since the COVID-19 pandemic, every passing season of the Premier League has seen faster sprinting and more "high-intensity actions." And with off-ball physical data like running distance or top speed becoming more accessible, scouting departments now possess more transparent measures of athleticism, leading to players' athletic qualities being valued more.

Rather than just affecting the head coach's team talk, these big-picture changes have a major effect on the skill sets that clubs look for when assembling their starting XIs. Let's take a look at five positions -- goalkeepers, center backs, fullbacks, central midfielders, and strikers -- to see what has changed and why.

Goalkeepers: Distribution and cross-claiming

New Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki has generated much buzz this season. One of his standout features has been his passing ability, playing quick passes to his center backs during the early buildup and exquisite floated long passes to Villa's forwards to escape pressure.

As impressive as his reflex saves are, Suzuki doesn't appear to be a great shot stopper. His "goals prevented" stats, based on post-shot expected goals, reveal that his shot-stopping numbers have hovered around that of the average major league goalkeeper over the past couple of seasons. In fact, in 2025-26, he prevented minus-0.4 goals per 90 minutes, implying that he did slightly worse than the average keeper last season.

However, his passing displays and his excellent cross-claiming make him a highly prized player, and his skill set epitomizes the state of today's goalkeeping.

When Pep Guardiola's Manchester City signed Gianluigi Donnarumma -- known for his shot-stopping abilities, but arguably an average distributor -- as their first-choice goalkeeper in summer 2025, it looked like elite soccer was once again prioritizing shot-stopping between the sticks. But the tactical conditions of soccer in the 2020s make ball-playing goalkeepers even more crucial than before; when teams are tasked with playing the ball past intense man-to-man presses, goalkeepers have more to do in the buildup phase.

Even the most aggressive man-to-man presses don't generally mark the goalkeeper, making keepers free options in the buildup. From this point, keepers are instrumental to playing quick passes around the box to try to bait the press for "artificial transitions" as well as with playing longer passes into space to relieve pressure and kick-start a direct attack.

As a result, the heyday of keepers primarily known for what they can do with their feet looks unlikely to recede anytime soon, with more intense pressing and more direct attacking arguably magnifying their value.

Meanwhile, although the number of open-play crosses that teams in the Big Five leagues play has decreased slightly since 2018, the ever-rising threat of set-play goals makes cross-claiming an especially valuable skill. The first-choice keepers at big clubs dominate the top of the leaderboard for cross-claiming statistics; Donnarumma ranked No. 1 for the highest percentage of crosses claimed in the Premier League last season, Barcelona's Joan García and Real Madrid's Thibaut Courtois ranked second and third, respectively, in last season's LaLiga campaign, and PSG's Lucas Chevalier ranked third in Ligue 1.

On the other hand, the keepers who populated the bottom of cross-claiming tables belong to either lower-table clubs or underperforming established sides like Tottenham Hotspur and Newcastle United. As valuable as goalkeepers' distribution is in 2026, it appears that the ability to claim crosses has become crucial to success between the sticks.

Center backs: Playmaking and pushing forward

In the 2015-16 Premier League season, the top five players who completed the most passes per 90 were Santi Cazorla, Cesc Fabregas, Bastian Schweinsteiger, Aaron Ramsey and Michael Carrick, with more central and attacking midfielders completing the top 10. In 2025-26, the top five were Rodri, Lewis Dunk, Curtis Jones, Trevoh Chalobah and William Saliba, with seven center backs making up the top 10.

A decade ago, central midfielders were at the heart of elite sides' passing moves, but today, especially in the Premier League, center backs are the primary passers in most sides.

In the Big Five leagues, center backs completed 19% more passes in the 2025-26 season than in 2018-19. Much of this has to do with intense man-to-man pressing systems, meaning that players positioned deeper have more prominent buildup duties. The 2020s have also seen nominal center backs become more involved in attacking play, taking up higher and wider positions. Attacking center backs are effective tools to dismantle mid-blocks, helping complicate marking duties with their movement.

This is easiest to do with wide center backs in a back three. Gian Piero Gasperini's Atalanta and Simone Inzaghi's Internazionale did this especially often. This season, Xabi Alonso's Chelsea and Gasperini's AS Roma are key examples, with the latter probably representing the most adventurous iteration of attacking center backs we've seen this century.

We can see some of this in back-four systems, too. Guardiola used John Stones as a center back who roved forward in possession at City, while Thiago Motta used Riccardo Calafiori and Jhon Lucumí as center backs with free roles.

As this decade progresses, the phrase "center back" might be encased in quotation marks more often.

Fullbacks: Rise of the underlap

Fullbacks often epitomize the tactical eras they find themselves in. The turn of the 2010s saw the rise of overlapping attacking fullbacks who move high up the pitch and outside wingers who cut inside with the ball. The mid-to-late 2010s saw the rise of high-intensity pressing, with high-possession sides using inverted fullbacks to provide security against counterattacks resulting from losing the ball. Meanwhile, the relative conservatism that followed the COVID-19 pandemic meant that nominal center backs were often deployed at fullback.

Today, we're seeing the rise of attacking fullbacks who underlap, making runs into the channels between opposition fullbacks and center backs, much like inverted wingers. As Caleb Gearty notes for SCOUTED, "the ability to receive the ball" is progressively becoming more highly valued for fullbacks. After getting in behind back lines, underlapping fullbacks can put in dangerous cutbacks and crosses from closer to goal, or take shots themselves.

In the case of back-three formations, this isn't a new phenomenon. For instance, Thomas Tuchel's Chelsea saw wingbacks Reece James and Ben Chilwell move inside and score goals, while Inzaghi used Federico Dimarco and Denzel Dumfries as goal-scoring threats at Inter.

But now, fullbacks in back-four systems are increasingly venturing forward and inside -- not just putting crosses in, but getting on the end of goal-scoring opportunities, too. Arsenal's Calafiori and Manchester City's Nico O'Reilly often make darting runs into the box and offer secondary goal threats. Spain's World Cup win saw Marc Cucurella and Pedro Porro underlap, pulling defenses apart.

Meanwhile, back-three systems feature wingbacks who pose greater goal-scoring threats than ever. Alonso's Chelsea are an instructive example -- they signed Pep Chavarría and Marco Palestra, but Alonso currently appears to favor the left-footed winger Pedro Neto at right wingback, who makes sharp runs into the box.

Why is this the case? In an age when defensive tactics are dominated by player-marking, the positional interchanges around the flanks (or "wide rotations") and unexpected diagonal darts forward from fullbacks can scramble player-marking duties and open up space -- especially when wingers find themselves closer to the sideline. As Billy Carpenter writes, sudden moves into the spaces in behind defenses can expose structural vulnerabilities in even the best mid-blocks.

Calafiori so far this season represents a great example, making well-timed runs in behind and receiving incisive through balls ...

... and creating goals like these.

Jamie Carragher once remarked that fullbacks are either failed wingers or failed center backs. The rise of inverted fullbacks would've allowed Carragher to add "failed midfielder" to his jibe, while today, a middling inside forward can consider a successful career as an underlapping attacking fullback.

Central midfielders: Large spaces and generalists

In 2026, the most expensive player archetype to sign in soccer appears to be the generalist midfielder. Of the 10 most expensive transfers this summer per Transfermarkt, six were central midfielders. And among the major moves in midfield that big clubs made this summer, most midfielders are do-it-all generalists who, at least in theory, contribute to passing, carrying, winning the ball back and sometimes crashing the box. These include Elliot Anderson, Sandro Tonali, Ayyoub Bouaddi, Bruno Guimarães, Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos.

This hasn't always been the case. By 2009, the box-to-box midfielder had become a dying breed, superseded by specialists in midfield. In the late 2010s, the rise of pressing meant that press-resistant ball carriers in midfield became increasingly valued, epitomized by the summer 2019 transfer window, which saw Frenkie de Jong, Tanguy Ndombele and Mateo Kovacic move for sums exceeding €40 million. But now, every big club is willing to spend astronomic sums on their own equivalent of Declan Rice or Moisés Caicedo; athletic midfielders who can cover lots of ground and do a bit of everything.

Counterintuitively, this might be happening because less of the game is happening in midfield. With the rise of situational player-marking, the middle third sees larger spaces opened up between lines of pressure, while space becomes more constricted in teams' own thirds. As a result, moving the ball from defense to midfield becomes a harder task, while the spaces opened up in the middle third mean teams don't pass the ball around as much there, instead moving the ball through it more quickly.

Jon Mackenzie and Jake Entwistle have discussed the relevance of "small spaces" -- where the player on the ball has little room to work with in the face of pressure -- and "large spaces" -- where players need to cover ground quickly, especially during transitions or when a line of pressure is broken -- in midfield, which influences how midfielder profiles are valued today. A player like Anderson, who combines small-space and large-space skills, becomes priceless, but the broader emphasis shifts from small-space specialists to large-space generalists who can cover ground and offer control in the center of the park.

As a result, affecting the pace of the attack, rather than just exerting control over space, becomes a key consideration in midfield. The rise of artificial transitions in response to pressing also means central midfielders are key to moving the ball from small spaces to large spaces, as Carlos Baleba did adeptly while at Brighton.

The middle of the park is integral to controlling a game of soccer, and as we're seeing the very notion of "control" change in the middle of the 2020s, the traits associated with the most highly valued midfielders are transformed, too.

Strikers: Physicality and pinning

While the first two decades of top-level soccer in the 21st century saw increasing versatility at the center forward position, the opposite is happening in the third decade. So far, the 2020s have seen taller, faster and stronger strikers being valued more than their smaller, more technical counterparts. Of course, Erling Haaland represents the platonic ideal of a striker -- in this era and in any other -- but the players who spearhead attacks in the middle of the 2020s tend to be 6-foot-2 or taller, and combine their size with pace.

Today's strikers are also less involved in link-up play than their equivalents at the turn of the 2020s, with the average striker in the Big Five leagues completing 16% fewer passes in 2025-26 than in 2018-19.

As discussed earlier, with attacks becoming more direct, the established strategy of pushing teams back and overwhelming defenses with patient play in the attacking third is falling out of fashion, which means strikers don't need to be as involved outside the penalty area. Instead, strikers increasingly spend most of the game pinning back defenders and stretching back lines, attempting to find space within settled defensive blocks. Plus, an increased emphasis on transitions correspondingly makes outlets to hit on the break becoming more valuable, and some extra size certainly comes in handy while trying to score goals from set pieces.

However, the players who currently lead most big clubs' front lines indicate the trend might be reversing at the upper echelons of the game. Harry Kane drops deeper than ever and conducts passing moves from midfield at Bayern, PSG won the Champions League with Ousmane Dembélé as a false 9 last season, Mikel Arteta appears to favor Kai Havertz up front over Viktor Gyokeres at Arsenal, and Barcelona currently deploy Raphinha at the No. 9 spot.

This might be because teams are finding alternate ways of manipulating player-marking strategies, picking holes in defenses with positional interchanges. By dropping deeper, a striker can bring the defender assigned to marking him along and create space for teammates. For example, in this case, João Pedro dropping deep to receive a throw-in pokes a hole for Morgan Rogers to run into, who in turn creates space for Cole Palmer's carry and goal.

For now, specialized, physically gifted strikers may have their time in the sun, but we're likely to see many approaches at the center forward position as the decade progresses.

What to make of 2026 trends

Many soccer fans view today's tactical landscape as being one of stasis or even regression. It's tempting to view the rise of directness and set pieces, as well as do-it-all midfielders and big strikers, as the return of older approaches. But this might be a reductive view; as Mackenzie notes in his book "The Spectre of Pep," presenting changes in the tactical landscape as purely being "cyclical" makes it "very difficult to speak of the 'new' in any meaningful way at all."

All the smaller tactical shifts we're seeing across the pitch are happening in relation to broader changes in the tactical environment of the 2020s. With the rise of man-to-man pressing approaches and the resulting revival of direct attacking, accompanied with the resurgence of ground-eating midfielders and big, physical strikers, these very same trends have brought about the rise of playmaking goalkeepers, attacking center backs, and underlapping fullbacks.

If a Premier League manager from 2006 drove a plutonium-powered DeLorean to 2026, he might find the first five minutes of play recognizable, but would be scandalized by the time he reaches the 10-minute mark. Welcome to elite soccer in the 2020s.

stories.headline: Singapore Grand Prix 2026: Race start time, how to watch, full schedule, predictions
stories.summary: Formula 1's original night race is back as drivers prepare for the ultimate challenge around the Marina Bay Circuit in Singapore.
stories.body:
Formula 1's original night race is back as drivers prepare for the ultimate challenge around the Marina Bay Circuit in Singapore.

It will also be the sixth and final sprint race of the season as Singapore hosts it for the first time.

Max Verstappen claimed his first victory of the season at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, while Kimi Antonelli extended his lead in the title championship to 84 points from George Russell.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the 17th round of the season.

- Bahrain GP was the worst indictment of F1's new engine regs yet

- Could Malaysia return to F1 calendar? The state of play despite Sepang travel chaos

- Max Verstappen wins disrupted Bahrain GP, Kimi Antonelli extends title lead as George Russell retires

Singapore Grand Prix schedule
All times in BST

Friday, October 9

Practice One: 9.30 a.m. - 10.30 a.m.

Sprint Qualifying: 1.30 p.m. - 2.14 p.m.

Saturday, October 10

Sprint: 10 a.m. - 11 a.m.

How to watch

Every practice and qualifying session as well as the race itself will be available to watch on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the Singapore Grand Prix will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Marina Bay Street Circuit

Singapore is one of the toughest challenges on the calendar for drivers due to the intense humidity and physically demanding nature of the circuit.

But this time round the drivers will have had a chance to get used to the humid conditions after racing in Malaysia for the Bahrain Grand Prix last weekend.

The Marina Bay Circuit has been on the calendar since 2008 and is one of the standout tracks. The race takes place at night with its breathtaking views of the city's skyline as cars make their way through the tight and twisty circuit.

Drivers can lose around 3kg in body weight after each race due to the amount they sweat.

Singapore Grand Prix

Circuit: Marina Bay Street Circuit; Singapore

Previous winners in Singapore

2014: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2015: Sebastian Vettel (Ferrari)

2016: Nico Rosberg (Mercedes)

2017: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2018: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2022: Sergio Pérez (Red Bull)

2023: Carlos Sainz (Ferrari)

2025: George Russell (Mercedes)

Other key stats

First F1 race: 2008

Lap record: 1:33.808 Lewis Hamilton (2025)

Most wins: Sebastian Vettel has the most wins with five (2011-2013, 2015 and 2019). From the current grid, Hamilton has four wins (2009, 2014, 2017-2018) and Fernando Alonso with two (2008 and 2010). Pérez (2022), Sainz (2023), Norris (2024) and Russell (2025) have all won a race each here.

Most poles: Vettel (2011, 2013, 2015, 2017) and Hamilton (2009, 2012, 2014, 2018) share the pole record with four each. From the current grid, Charles Leclerc (2019, 2022) has had two pole positions here.

Weather forecast

The weather for the Singapore Grand Prix is set to be thundery showers and light winds throughout the weekend, with highs of 34°C on Friday. The temperature is forecast to drop a degree for the remainder of the weekend.

What happened last time out?
Russell claimed pole position in Singapore last year and crossed the line 0.182 seconds clear of Red Bull's Verstappen, with McLaren's Oscar Piastri behind.

Russell took his second win of the season, but there was plenty of other drama during the race, especially at McLaren.

Norris, who started in fifth, knocked into Piastri when trying to pass him in the first corner. Piastri managed to gain some ground towards the end of the race, but he had to settle for fourth on the day McLaren lifted the trophy for the constructors' title.

Piastri's drivers' championship lead to Norris was separated by only 22 points with six races left of the season.

Who will win this year?

One to watch this weekend is Red Bull and Verstappen after he won the race last weekend. The team brought major upgrades two races ago and improvements to its overall performance has been evident.

Russell, who suffered a major blow to his championship hopes after retiring last time out, will be looking to maximise the points on offer across the weekend.

Mercedes are expected to be strong, while Ferrari are quick in cornering speed. Hamilton has won four times here, so could be a threat. McLaren's Norris and Piastri fell under the radar and struggled for pace in Malaysia.

All will be to play for under the lights in Singapore as we head into the business end of the season.

stories.headline: What's next: Will Silva's first title defense be against Shevchenko?
stories.summary: The most likely opponent and a wild card for the winners and losers on the UFC 332 main card.
stories.body:
The UFC has a new women's flyweight champion for the first time in over two years following the UFC 332 main event in Salt Lake City on Saturday night. And with a new champion comes brand-new matchups. After winning the belt via unanimous decision over Wang Cong, Natalia Silva will have no shortage of challengers looking for their shot at gold.

Also on the UFC 332 fight card, rising men's bantamweight contender Payton Talbott made quick work of former two-time men's flyweight champion Deiveson Figueiredo in the co-main event. Talbott could take on a top-ranked contender in his next Octagon appearance. And a handful of young prospects earned impressive first-round knockout victories.

Here's what's next for the top stars of UFC 332.

Natalia Silva, women's flyweight champion

Who should be next: Valentina Shevchenko

The state of the UFC's women's divisions is not ideal. We haven't seen a bantamweight title fight all year, due to injuries to Kayla Harrison. Mackenzie Dern is the strawweight champion, but (fair or not) there is a pretty significant need for her to fight Zhang Weili to validate her standing as the top 115-pound fighter in the world, since Zhang vacated her belt, never lost it in competition. Now the same is true of the flyweight title. Silva has the longest active win streak at 125 pounds and might be the best in the world, but she'll battle for that perception until she fights Shevchenko. We'll have to see how long Shevchenko is out, but this fight needs to happen as soon as possible.

Wild card: Erin Blanchfield

Blanchfield has looked like future champion material since she debuted with the UFC at 22 years old in 2021. She's now five years into her UFC career, and she is 8-1 with one learning experience in the form of a five-round decision loss to Manon Fiorot in 2024. She's still only 27 and could well prove to be the future of this weight class. She's got a tough matchup scheduled against Jasmine Jasudavicius on Oct. 17. If she gets past that unscathed, the UFC could easily book her with Silva as soon as possible, instead of waiting for Shevchenko.

Payton Talbott, men's bantamweight
Who should be next: Sean O'Malley

It has to be done. O'Malley was once the darling of the bantamweight division. Now it's Talbott, and it's hard to deny this matchup. Now, the UFC is almost certainly already looking at O'Malley for an upcoming title fight. Especially if Petr Yan defeats Merab Dvalishvili at UFC 333 later this month, O'Malley is the favorite to face Yan next. But if UFC fans were polled, the more anticipated fight might honestly be O'Malley vs. Talbott. Not to get out of control here, but this could headline a numbered event.

Wild card: Farid Basharat

This would be the anti-O'Malley booking. The UFC doesn't love that Basharat has mostly decisions on his record -- so much so that there's been some uncertainty about his security with the promotion. He's ranked in the top 10 by the UFC but in a spot to defend his spot (not attack). This is the kind of athlete who might need to fight down the rankings. Enter Talbott.

Ateba Gautier, middleweight
Who should be next: Loser of Bo Nickal vs. Joe Pyfer on Dec. 12

Hear me out: Gautier's hype train took a major, major hit with the first-round knockout loss to Roman Kopylov. There's no way around it. He took a step up in competition, and fell very flat. In this situation, the UFC can quietly step him back to the prelims somewhere -- or it can create a story. Gautier's stock took a hit but he is still extremely dangerous. There's still intrigue attached to him. Nickal is coming off a strong win at the White House over Kyle Daukaus, but there are still question marks around him. Pyfer is riding high after a finish of Israel Adesanya in his last bout. Whoever loses between Nickal and Pyfer would still be in position for a compelling bout. What's more compelling than this? There is still a way for the UFC to use what's left of the hype around Gautier and make a fight fans will want to watch.

Wild card: Loser of Daukaus vs. Marc-Andre Barriault on Oct. 17

This would be an appropriate next step that would teach us more about Gautier. Kopylov is a legitimate (for lack of a better word) gatekeeper, and Daukaus and Andre Barriault are also proven veterans. Either would challenge Gautier and offer him a chance at redemption.

stories.headline: Five grand finalists named in Samoa's RLWC squad
stories.summary: Ben Gardiner has been denied the chance to call up Payne Haas, but Samoa's Rugby League World Cup squad remains filled with NRL talent.
stories.body:
Francis Manuleleua and Jermaine McEwen have been rewarded for their starring roles in Newcastle's run to the NRL Grand Final with the back-row duo named in Samoa's Rugby League World Cup squad.

Even without Payne Haas, as the South Sydney-bound prop undergoes hand surgery, the Samoan squad is still packed with talent.

Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow, Brian To'o and Stephen Crichton are all included, along with Sydney Roosters front-rower Spencer Leniu following his exploits in the NRL Grand Final.

Jarome Luai will co-captain the side with Parramatta prop Junior Paulo.

"One of the great things rugby league does is bring people together," Toa Samoa coach Ben Gardiner said.

"As we build towards our first World Cup game, we want to thank all Samoans around the world for their ongoing support.

"Your blessings and prayers are welcomed.

"Whether you are in Samoa, elsewhere around the world, taking part in a parade or marching into the ground, we see you and thank you for your love and support."

Roosters hooker Benaiah Ioelu is likely to share hooking duties with Jazz Tevaga, who won the Super League Grand Final with Wakefield last week.

Gardiner's side will open their campaign against France in Parramatta before facing Papua New Guinea in Port Moresby and rounding out their pool stage fixtures against Tonga.

Samoa squad: Shawn Blore, Stephen Crichton, Sua Fa'alogo, Clayton Faulalo, Chanel Harris-Tavita, Benaiah Ioelu, Connelly Lemuelu, Spencer Leniu, Jarome Luai, Francis Manuleleua, Deine Mariner, Ata Mariota, Greg Marzhew, Jermaine McEwen, Francis Molo, Junior Paulo, Pasami Saulo, Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow, Izack Tago, Jazz Tevaga, Brian To'o, Enari Tuala, Ronald Volkman.

stories.headline: Small-ball Rays beat the sloppy Yankees 5-2 for a 2-0 lead in AL Division Series
stories.summary: — The pesky Rays put all the pressure on the big, bad New York Yankees.
stories.body:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- — The pesky Rays put all the pressure on the big, bad New York Yankees.


Richie Palacios hit a two-run single in a four-run fifth inning and Tampa Bay took advantage of New York's sloppy defense, beating Cam Schlittler and the Yankees 5-2 on Monday night to take a 2-0 lead in their AL Division Series.


The Rays are one victory from reaching the American League Championship Series. Game 3 in the best-of-five playoff is Wednesday night at Yankee Stadium.


“That’s a byproduct of having a really good clubhouse and a bunch of selfless teammates,” Rays manager Kevin Cash said. “They don’t care who gets it done. They just want to get it done. The biggest cheerleaders are coming from the guys within the dugout. Good teams do not rely on just one or two people. We rely on all nine in the lineup, the guys on the bench and certainly our entire pitching staff.”


Ben Rice homered twice for the Yankees, who are on the verge of elimination — which would extend their drought without a World Series championship to 17 seasons. They were dominated by Drew Rasmussen in the series opener and have scored just two runs in two playoff games against the AL East champion Rays with three-time AL MVP Aaron Judge out of the lineup due to a calf injury.


“Well, we’ve got to win. We’ve got to play the first inning of Game 3,” Yankees manager Aaron Boone said. “We’ve got to come out and play well. So we’ve responded all year. We need to do it again. Obviously, we need to play better and it starts with just one at a time. I don’t even get ahead of myself and win three. We’ve got to go win one and we’ve got to play better Wednesday night to make that happen.”


The small-ball Rays chased Schlittler, the likely AL Cy Young Award winner, in the fifth aided by New York's defensive miscues.


Jonathan Aranda lined a single to start the inning and Junior Caminero ripped a double to right-center. With the infield drawn-in except second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr., who was standing several feet further back on the dirt, Liam Hicks hit a slow bouncer to second that scored Aranda for a 2-1 lead. Chisholm's only play was at first because he wasn't all the way in like the rest of the infielders.


Chandler Simpson then hit a grounder that shortstop George Lombard Jr. flubbed, scoring Caminero to make it 3-1. It was initially ruled a hit and then changed to an error and eventually a fielder's choice. Brent Headrick replaced Schlittler and struck out Victor Mesa Jr. After Simpson stole second, Jonny DeLuca reached on a grounder when Lombard's throw to first was wide for New York's fourth error.


Palacios followed with a hard single to center that increased Tampa Bay's lead to 5-1.


“It was just one of those games things kind of compiled and stacked up on top of each other," Lombard said. “It wasn't ideal. We put ourselves in a bad spot.”


That was plenty of support for one of the best bullpens in the majors.


Freddy Peralta allowed one run and three hits in 4 2/3 innings, Cam Booser pitched out of a bases-loaded jam in the fifth and Ian Seymour gave up one run in three innings. Bryan Baker finished with a perfect ninth for his second save in two games.


Schlittler, who was 14-6 with a 1.95 ERA and dominated Boston in the opener of the wild-card round, lasted 4 1/3 innings. He allowed four runs — two earned — and six hits while striking out only two.


Rice sent a 2-2 changeup into the right-field seats to tie it at 1 in the fourth, ending New York's scoreless drought in the ALDS. Rice hit 41 homers in the regular season. His drive awakened Yankees fans in the ballpark, who were drowned out by Rays fans until that point.


But a sellout crowd of 40,226 was mostly full of cowbell-ringing Rays fans who reveled in New York's misery.


Peralta retired the first two batters in the fifth before Austin Wells ripped a double and Ryan McMahon walked. Booser replaced Peralta and walked Rice to load the bases, but the lefty escaped when Cody Bellinger flied out to the warning track in center.


The Yankees made three errors in the first inning but Schlittler limited the Rays to one run. New York became the first team to commit three errors in the first inning of a postseason game since the Oakland Athletics in Game 1 of the 1975 AL Championship Series against Boston, according to Sportsnet Stats.


Off the catwalk
Yankees rookie Spencer Jones hit a towering flyball off a catwalk at quirky Tropicana Field that was caught by Mesa for an out in the second inning. Jones kept running around the bases as the ball rattled around and fell to Mesa, who ran over from right field to make the catch in center. DeLuca thought he was camped under it in center but started pointing upward when the ball hit one of the two rings high above the field and below the roof. Mesa caught it several feet in front of DeLuca. Umpires conferred and confirmed the out, per the stadium’s ground rules.


Up next
Yankees LHP Max Fried (5-5, 2.80 ERA) and Rays RHP Nick Martinez (15-6, 3.10) are the projected starters for Game 3.

stories.headline: Atlanta's jabs at New Orleans after MNF top Week 4 trolls
stories.summary: The calendar shifted to October, and the trolls are becoming a little more impactful, led by the Atlanta Falcons.
stories.body:
Welcome to the first weekend of October, when the games get a little more meaningful and the trolls follow suit. Week 4 of the NFL season was further proof of that.

The Atlanta Falcons dominated the New Orleans Saints 45-24 on "Monday Night Football," thanks to a standout performance from their backfield.

Atlanta put up a whopping 420 yards, led by 145 rushing yards by Bijan Robinson, who also added two scores. His fellow running back Brian Robinson Jr. put up three touchdowns. The Falcons' five rushing touchdowns tied a franchise record. They are the sixth pair of teammates who each had multiple rushing touchdowns in a "Monday Night Football" game. The Falcons' lone passing touchdown occurred when quarterback Michael Penix Jr. connected with wide receiver Jahan Dotson for a 31-yard score.

With the Falcons-Saints rivalry being one of the fiercest in the league, it only made sense that Atlanta poked fun after the victory -- multiple times. The Falcons captioned their post: "Marched in," a nod to the Saints' anthem, "When the Saints Go Marching In."

The Falcons then resurfaced a video in which a Saints fan motioned a choking sign at Falcons players as they entered halftime with a lead, indicating that Atlanta would eventually lose. The original video had the caption: "This Saints fan potentially could have an all-time clip for the second half," to which the Falcons quipped postgame with: "He did not."

Here are the other top trolls from Week 4.

Dallas Cowboys 34, Houston Texans 30
The Dallas Cowboys defeated the Houston Texans on the road. Facing a four-point deficit with 2:23 left, Dallas went on an 11-play, 74-yard drive that concluded with a 12-yard touchdown catch by wide receiver CeeDee Lamb.

It put the Cowboys up for good and capped a stellar performance from Lamb. He had a whopping 17 catches -- second most in franchise history -- for 189 yards. It's the most receptions by any player since Keenan Allen had 18 in Week 3 of the 2023 season, according to ESPN Research.

Dallas had clever jabs lined up for the in-state matchup. The Cowboys referenced country star Ella Langley's hit track, "Choosin' Texas," in a social media post, adding "Dallas" ahead of "Texas."

Then, Dallas put a spin on the opening sequence from the sitcom "King of the Hill," which is set in Texas. The illustration featured Lamb, Dak Prescott, wide receiver George Pickens and safety Caleb Downs hanging out together with "Kings of the State" written above them.

Carolina Panthers 32, Detroit Lions 26
It required one final stop, but the Panthers survived for a "Sunday Night Football" win against the Lions.

Carolina held a six-point lead when Detroit regained possession with 2:06 left. Four plays later, the Lions turned it over on downs, clinching the Panthers' victory. Panthers quarterback Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns -- both to wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan, who had 14 catches for 192 yards. Their teammate, running back Chuba Hubbard, had 122 yards on the ground and two scores.

Carolina understood the assignment postgame when poking fun at Detroit. It shared an image of a Panther standing on a ledge and growling over a lion, writing in the caption: "The Lion's king."

Seattle Seahawks 30, Los Angeles Chargers 23
Seattle held on to beat Los Angeles in a bounce-back victory.

The Chargers had a chance to tie the score with 1:42 remaining, but the Seahawks sacked quarterback Justin Herbert to force a fumble, which they recovered to secure the win. Seattle forced four turnovers -- three came from Herbert and two led to touchdowns.

The Seahawks had multiple lightning- and charging-related trolls after the win.

Their first post was simple with the caption: "Lights Out," a reference to the nickname of Chargers legend Shawne Merriman. Seattle's victory comic included a robot out of charge. Seahawks defensive end Leonard Williams was labeled "The Lightning Thief," the title of a popular Rick Riordan novel. Then there was an image of a charging cord with tattered wires, captioned "0% battery," and another of a charging error with safety Nick Emmanwori sacking Herbert in the background.

Los Angeles Rams 24, Philadelphia Eagles 20
Los Angeles stormed back late to beat Philadelphia on the road.

The Rams outscored the Eagles 14-0 in the second half. The winning touchdown came on a 7-yard run by Kyren Williams with 1:10 left. The Eagles then had a turnover on downs, giving the Rams the ball and the win.

Even though the result was still up in the air, Los Angeles soft launched its troll with a post earlier in the day. The Rams shared an image of their players with "Rams in Philadelphia" written above them in a font evoking the hit comedy "Abbott Elementary," which is set in Philadelphia.

Just over five hours later, Los Angeles posted a test paper with scantron bubbles filled in to spell out "W."

San Francisco 49ers 24, Denver Broncos 14
The 49ers remain undefeated following a win against the Broncos.

San Francisco's defense shined, allowing just one touchdown and 296 total yards to Denver. The 49ers' offense played its part, too, specifically the offensive line -- the team has yet to give up a sack this season. The Niners are the first team to allow zero sacks through four games since the 2005 Indianapolis Colts, according to ESPN Research.

The Broncos' home stadium is Empower Field at Mile High, and even though the 49ers won at home, they highlighted the "mile high" component with a jab.

Jacksonville Jaguars 22, Cincinnati Bengals 17
Jacksonville's wire-to-wire win over Cincinnati prompted a simple, yet effective, troll.

Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence had 223 passing yards and one score, and Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow threw for 428 yards, one touchdown plus two interceptions. Cincinnati put up a whopping 437 yards of offense but had only two touchdowns to show for it.

In a battle between Jaguars and Bengals, Jacksonville highlighted its win by writing "Jungle Cats" in its postgame caption.

Cleveland Browns 27, Pittsburgh Steelers 24
The Browns have won three straight games for the first time since 2023 after defeating the Steelers on "Thursday Night Football."

Pittsburgh tied the score with 1:42 remaining, but Cleveland responded by kicking a winning field goal with 10 ticks left. As a result, Deshaun Watson became the second Browns quarterback since 1970 to lead three straight winning drives in the fourth quarter or overtime, according to ESPN Research.

At first glance, Cleveland's Minecraft-themed post after the win seemed something ordinary. But it was a reference to former Pittsburgh head coach Mike Tomlin revealing his Minecraft world Wednesday. The Browns capitalized on the moment by building out an "L" in Minecraft blocks and writing: "Pittsburgh was defeated by the Dawg Pound."

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little earlier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Monday, Oct. 5
TRADE PERIOD OPENS
Merrett finally becomes a Hawk

After attempting to join Hawthorn last year, Zach Merrett has finally been traded from Essendon to the Hawks.

Hawthorn have sent picks 15, 25 and a 2028 second-round pick in exchange for the 31-year-old.

Merrett leaves the Bombers a week after winning a record-equaling seventh Crichton Medal, three All-Australian blazers, and 274 games.

Pendlebury becomes a Sun

AFL games record holder Scott Pendlebury is officially a Sun after Gold Coast and Collingwood agreed on a trade for the 38-year-old veteran.

Pendlebury, a two-time premiership player, heads to the Suns in exchange for pick No. 65 in this year's draft.

"It's an exciting group here at the SUNS and the opportunity to bring a few different ideas and also learn from a great group of coaches and players is one I'm really looking forward to," Pendlebury told the Suns.

"This side is one I've watched from afar and really admired. I've got a bit of knowledge about the industry so I'm here to play my role and help this squad continue to develop."

Jesse Hogan traded from GWS to Collingwood

Out-of-favour Giants forward Jesse Hogan has made the switch to Collingwood in exchange for pick 75.

The 31-year-old won the Coleman Medal in 2024 but has been unable to recapture his best form at the Giants in the two years since.

Magpies list boss Justin Leppitsch said Hogan would be a valuable addition.

"On behalf of everyone at Collingwood, I'd like to warmly welcome Jesse to Collingwood. Jesse has established himself as one of the competition's premier key forwards and we're excited to see him bring his experience and talent to our club," he said.

"His aerial presence inside forward-50 and his consistency as a goal-kicker make him a genuine threat.

"Like Lachie (Neale), Jesse has a passion to teach the next generation and will make a great addition to our club."

Saturday, Oct. 3
Bulldogs seal free-agency signing of key defender

The Western Bulldogs have finally snagged the key defender they need, securing Adelaide backman Jordon Butts as an unrestricted free agent.

The Bulldogs are set for a bumper AFL trade period headlined by working through a deal for Port Adelaide superstar Zak Butters, ahead of a 2027 season where the club will have high expectations.

But after seeing off Carlton's advances to keep hold of defender Buku Khamis, the Bulldogs have filled a major area of need by adding 26-year-old Butts.

Adelaide will receive a second-round compensation selection, currently pick No.33, in this year's draft.

-- AAP

Friday, Oct. 2
FREE AGENCY OPEN
Three-peat Lion locks in Magpies move

Lachie Neale has sealed his high-profile switch to Collingwood, with Brisbane teasing the dual Brownlow medallist on his way out the door.

The AFL approved Neale signing a three-year deal with the Magpies on Friday afternoon, closing out the first day of free agency.

The 33-year-old ball-winner leaves as an unrestricted free agent after the Lions clinched a third straight flag with their stunning seven-point grand final victory over Fremantle.

-- AAP

Greene on his way to the Cats

Toby Greene will join Geelong as an unrestricted free agent on a three-year deal, re-partnering with former Giants teammate Jeremey Cameron.

The paperwork was lodged to the AFL on Friday morning.

The Giants receive band three compensation for Greene, which is currently pick No. 26 in the upcoming draft.

Greene departs the Giants with his name etched in the club's record books, sitting first in games played for the club with a tally of 282 games, as well as leading the club's all-time goalkicking tally with 450 majors.

Briggs now a Tiger

Richmond has landed GWS ruck Kieren Briggs as an unrestricted free agent.

Briggs' move to the Tigers was confirmed just hours after the free agency window opened on Friday.

Briggs played 88 games for GWS after joining the club as the No.34 pick in the 2018 draft.

Amartey officially joins the Blues

Free agency has opened with a bang, with out-of-favour key forward Joel Amartey committing to Carlton.

Details are still to come on the length of contract, and Sydney's compensation.

Hawthorn father-son recommits despite interest

Calsher Dear has made a shock decision to re-sign with the Hawks for two years, despite being out of favour thorughout 2026.

The 20-year-old has kicked 39 goals from 31 games, but found himself behind Jack Gunston, Mitch Lewis and Mabior Chol. With Gunston signed on and Suns forward Ben King expected to sign with the Hawks as well, there were questions about whether Dear would get enough opportunity at his childhood club.

Hawks list boss Mark McKenzie said the club was "really pleased" that Dear had recommitted.

"He remains an important part of what we are trying to achieve as a club," he said.

"Following his debut season, Calsher showed us all the special talent that he is, but as a key tall at 21 years of age, we've needed to be patient with his progression.

"Having battled several injuries over his first three seasons in the system, we are very excited about what the future holds for Calsher with a strong pre-season under his belt and greater continuity into 2027 and beyond."

Thursday, Oct. 1
Goater set to make cross-city switch

North Melbourne defender Josh Goater is set to join the Hawks after requesting a trade on Thursday.

Having played just 18 games, the 23-year-old had fallen out of favour after an injury-hit run in his time at North.

Premiership Lion requests trade

The Brisbane Lions have confirmed Sam Marshall has requested a trade to St Kilda.

"The Brisbane Lions confirm premiership midfielder Sam Marshall has requested to be traded to St Kilda," the Lions said in a statement.

"Marshall has played 13 games, including the 2025 Premiership, across two seasons since being selected in the first round of the 2024 draft as a graduate of the Youi Brisbane Lions Academy.

"The club respects Marshall's request to be traded, and will work towards facilitating an outcome that best reflects true value to the Brisbane Lions for the 20-year-old."

Tuesday, Sept. 29
Neale informs Lions he intends to join Collingwood

Two-time Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale has told Brisbane he will depart the club as an unrestricted free agent and sign a three-year deal with Collingwood.

Aware that Neale intended to leave at the end of the year, the Lions never offered him a new contract.

The paperwork for the deal is expected to be formalised as early as Friday when the free agency period opens.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: Jordan Pickford ignored give-way sign, almost caused crash, court hears
stories.summary: England goalkeeper Jordan Pickford nearly caused a crash with two other cars during a bout of careless driving in his £200,000 Lamborghini supercar, a court has heard.
stories.body:
England goalkeeper Jordan Pickford nearly caused a crash with two other cars during a bout of careless driving in his £200,000 Lamborghini supercar, a court has heard.

The 32-year-old was pulled over by police after ignoring a give-way sign, forcing two cars to slam on the brakes, and then speeding off into the distance.

The incident happened in the upmarket Cheshire town of Knutsford on April 14, sparking a criminal prosecution for driving without due care or attention.

Pickford, who has 336 appearances for Everton and 92 England caps, has pleaded guilty to the charge and requested a court hearing to explain his mitigation.

According to court documents, Pc Cecil Ricardo, from Cheshire Police, said he had just left the station when he saw Pickford's blue Lamborghini Urus complete with personalised number plates.

"I was stationary on Bexton Road, Knutsford, waiting for traffic signals to turn green," he wrote.

"I then witnessed a blue Lamborghini Urus driving along Princess Street.

"It reached the junction with Toft Road, completely ignored the give way lines and pulled onto Toft Road causing two vehicles to slam on their brakes to avoid a collision.

"The Lamborghini then sped down Toft Road, Knutsford."

Pc Ricardo said he activated his lights and siren to set off in pursuit of the Lamborghini, noticing he was driving at 50mph while the Lamborghini "was still pulling away."

"The speed limit on that stretch of Toft Road, Knutsford, is 30mph," he noted.

The officer said Pickford appeared to notice the chasing police car and pulled over.

Pickford pleaded guilty in writing in the Single Justice Procedure and told Warrington Magistrates Court: "I would like to attend court to put forward my mitigation."

His case was formally adjourned last week until a hearing at Chester Magistrates' Court on Dec. 7.

Pickford, who started his career at Sunderland before loan spells at six clubs including Burton, Bradford and Preston, has featured for England at the 2018, 2022 and 2026 World Cups, and was in goal for the country's Euro 2020 and 2024 final appearances.

stories.headline: Nigerian connection runs through Mystics rise as Kiki Iriafen breaks out in playoff run
stories.summary: Fresh from helping team USA win the World Cup last month, Kiki Iriafen's second WNBA season ended with a first round elimination to the Atlanta Dream.
stories.body:
Fresh from helping USA win the World Cup last month, Kiki Iriafen's second WNBA season ended with a first round elimination to the Atlanta Dream, but finishing the game with yet another double-double was an indication of just how quickly the Nigerian-American forward has grown into a central piece of the Washington Mystics' present.

Iriafen helped herself to 15 points and 16 rebounds in Washington's 93-75 loss to the Atlanta Dream, completing her first postseason with double-doubles in both games of the first-round series for an average of 15 points and 15 rebounds in the playoffs after a regular season in which she emerged as Washington's leading rebounder and one of their top three scorers.

Alongside her for much of that run was Michaela Onyenwere - another Nigerian-American forward whose contribution came from a different place. The 2021 WNBA Rookie of the Year came to Washington with five seasons of league experience to help the youngest roster in the WNBA and became enough of a veteran voice that her teammates began calling her "Coach Mic."

And just like she did on her Draft night when strutting it out in a dress that reflected her Nigerian heritage, Iriafen says she is driven by the Nigerian spirit

"My Nigerian heritage has been something that I've always wanted to promote," she said. "Michaela and I were just talking about what should we do. Like, we should go celebrate. But it's super special. My Nigerian heritage has been something that I've always wanted to promote. I am Nigerian American, but I feel like both sides of me are equally as important to me."

Together, both have given Washington the Nigerian connection within a team that improved from 16 wins in 2025 to a franchise-record 28 this season and returned to the playoffs for the first time since 2023.

Iriafen's rise, to go with the likes of USA teammate Sonia Citron, and Shakira Austin, was at the heart of that improvement.

After averaging 13.3 points and 8.5 rebounds as a rookie, the 23-year-old increased those numbers to 15.3 points and 9.5 rebounds this season while shooting better than 50% from the field. She finished behind Austin and Citron in scoring and led the Mystics in rebounding, narrowly ahead of Austin.

She also recorded a Mystics single-season record 23 double-doubles, and earned a second consecutive All-Star selection - numbers that helped get her onto Team USA's World Cup roster.

The postseason provided another test - one that Iriafen confronted head on, even if it was her first experience.

Foul trouble in Game 1 meant she played only 23 minutes against Atlanta, but still finished with 15 points and 14 rebounds. Nine of those rebounds came on the offensive end, tying a Washington franchise record for offensive rebounds in a game and helping the Mystics outrebound the Dream 50-31.

"I really felt like I wasn't able to help my team in the first half, so I wanted to do that for my teammates," Iriafen said.

Game 2 was much better, as she stayed on the floor for more than 35 minutes. Her 30 rebounds over the two games were the second-most by a player through her first two WNBA playoff games.

The numbers continued a progression that began almost immediately after Washington selected her with the No. 4 pick in the 2025 draft. Initially, the Mystics leaned heavily on Iriafen's rebounding, transition running and ability to finish around the basket. Now, her offensive responsibilities have gradually expanded to include more post touches, screening actions and opportunities to make decisions with the ball.

Her development has also come alongside Citron - Washington's other cornerstone from the 2025 draft. Citron led the Mystics in playoff scoring with 25 points in each game against Atlanta, while Iriafen controlled the glass.

The partnership leaves Washington with two young players who have already translated regular-season production into the postseason - one that coach Sydney Johnson was pleased with as he singled both out for praise.

"I'm sitting beside two players who played their first playoff games, and there was a lot of good stuff out there," he said. "I'm immensely disappointed for the result, but I also think what this group has accomplished and how the DC community has rallied around this group has been amazing. They've written history. I am excited to take this first step forward with Kiki and Sonia and our whole group."

For Iriafen, that development has unfolded alongside an identity she has repeatedly said matters a lot to her.

"Being Nigerian is huge for me," Iriafen told House of Victory earlier this year. "It's my culture, it's a big part of who I am.

"There are so many young Nigerian hoopers and young Nigerians that I'm an inspiration to and I just want to showcase that being Nigerian is cool."

That connection was there well before she played her first WNBA game. Who can forget Kiki owning the show at the 2025 WNBA draft in a custom dress designed by Nigerian designer Nneka Alexander, while accompanied by members of her family equally attired in traditional Nigerian clothing?

"My parents always say Naija no dey carry last," she said. "So I feel like in everything that I do, I try to strive for that. So that's kind of the motto of my life.

"Something in Nigeria is the resources aren't always as equal, but just understanding that it doesn't matter how you get there, there's still an opportunity. There's still a way. So I just really want to carry myself with class and really truly be a great role model."

The draft took her to Washington, which offered an even bigger connection to Nigeria, with its huge Nigerian population.

A year later, the Mystics added Onyenwere, whose route to the capital was considerably longer. Selected sixth overall by New York in 2021, Onyenwere won WNBA Rookie of the Year before stops with Phoenix and Chicago. Washington signed her to a multiyear deal this year and immediately installed her in a starting lineup filled with younger players.

Onyenwere, 26 years old when the season began, was the oldest player on the roster.

"We call her 'Coach Mic.' She knows what she's talking about," Iriafen said. "She's a great leader, great teammate and great person."

The connection between them predates the Mystics. They first crossed paths when Iriafen was a high school prospect considering UCLA and Onyenwere was playing for the Bruins.

Their Nigerian heritage provided another common thread. Onyenwere's father Peter competed for Nigeria in track and field, and her grandmother became one of the memorable images of the 2021 WNBA draft when she danced in traditional Nigerian clothing behind Onyenwere during a television interview when her name was called.

"I am just so proud to be Nigerian, and I never let anyone forget it," Onyenwere said. "I make sure I let people know I am Nigerian because it is a big part of who I am.

"From Draft Night, I was getting messages from young Nigerian kids who are in Nigeria, saying you are an inspiration. You don't really think those things until you see those messages. Like, I am influencing people in a different continent."

Both women have also represented the United States internationally - a clear sign of the dual identity they have carried and basked in through their basketball careers. Iriafen helped the United States win the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup, appearing in four games during the Americans' unbeaten run to the title.

Onyenwere represented USA Basketball in both 3x3 and 5-on-5 competition in 2019. She played on the American 3x3 circuit and later helped the United States win silver at the Pan American Games.

Nigeria did attempt to bring Onyenwere into the D'Tigress program for the 2024 Paris Olympics, but she was unable to join the team after failing to receive clearance in time.

In adding to the Nigerian connection, her role in Washington this season has been more about helping to provide stability around a young core.

Onyenwere averaged 9.0 points during the regular season while starting alongside Iriafen, Austin and Citron. She scored eight points in the opening playoff loss to Atlanta before adding 12 in Game 2.

Washington's season ended there, but Iriafen's first experience of playoff basketball provided another marker in a second season in which her responsibilities and production grew and both playoff games provided a clear measure of how far her role has expanded and where Washington could take it next.

She finished the two-game series averaging 15 points and 15 rebounds, with 13 offensive rebounds, after leading Washington in rebounding during the regular season and establishing career highs in both scoring and rebounding.

"This whole season has just been just a learning process for me," Iriafen said after Game 2. "It was nothing like my first season.

"I feel like just even during my undergrad, doing tough majors and still being a professional athlete, just showcasing that, whatever you put your mind to that you can do it."

For the Mystics, the next part of that learning process will be figuring out how much more Iriafen can handle. They already have one of the league's most productive young rebounders and an increasingly reliable interior scorer. Her three assists in Game 2 also offered a glimpse of how her role could expand as a passer and decision-maker.

Onyenwere, meanwhile, provided an experienced voice alongside her during that development, four years after becoming WNBA Rookie of the Year herself, giving the Mystics a Nigerian-American one-two punch.

The season may have ended earlier than they or the Mystics wanted, but it also provided a silver lining, with Washington back in the playoffs and Iriafen having experienced the stage that she wanted, even if she failed to conquer it. For now.

"Playoffs are the biggest stage," Iriafen said after Game 1. "This is the stage we want to be on."

On the evidence of this run, it is one that she will be returning to for the foreseeable future. And she will continue to be driven by that Naija no dey carry last spirit.
